title: When is the highest common factor one of the two numbers?
description: The pair six and eighteen has the highest common factor six, which is one of the two numbers. Three more pairs show the pattern, and the letter n with five n shows it for every such pair. Keeko doubts this and thinks the highest common factor must be smaller than both numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: the highest common factor is one of the two numbers exactly when one number is a factor of the other. Watch for students who think the highest common factor must be smaller than both numbers.

source: Find three more pairs where the HCF is one of the two numbers, and describe all such pairs.
video_script.why: The child can find a highest common factor but has not noticed when it equals one of the two numbers.
video_script.substitution: If the smaller number goes into the bigger one, the smaller number is the biggest factor they share.
video_script.anchor: The pair 6 and 18 written side by side, with the number 6 fitting into 18 three times.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a shared factor must be smaller than both numbers, so five and twenty seem to break the pattern. Five goes into twenty, so five is the biggest shared factor and is itself one of the numbers.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factor of n and five n is n

final_answer.value: The HCF is one of the numbers exactly when one number is a factor of the other; for n and 5n it is n
final_answer.spoken: one number is a factor of the other

never_show: HCF is always smaller than both numbers, marked right
maths_rules: 6 and 18: 18 = 6 × 3, HCF = 6, which is one of the two numbers
5 and 20: the factors of 5 are 1 and 5, both go into 20, HCF = 5
the HCF is one of the two numbers exactly when the smaller goes into the bigger, so one number is a factor of the other and the other is a multiple of it
algebra: 5n = 5 × n, so n goes into 5n and the HCF of n and 5n is n
